gaps.text: In-line measurement of Temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (A combined MIR-ATR and Raman probe would measure the same small spot, so both methods see the same material; two separate probes used alternately cannot guarantee this. The two data streams must be brought to a common time step and autoscaled before fusion, and each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. This option is worth pursuing only if the fused model beats the best single method on independent runs.)
No supplied source gives detection limits or accuracy figures for glucose or lactate in cell culture medium.
No supplied source covers cleaning, fouling or sterilisation requirements for a cell-culture process probe.

items.finding: The review states that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an aqueous cell-culture medium, this suggests that temperature control or measurement may be needed to reduce spectral variation; consider testing temperature stability and whether an in-line temperature sensor is required.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote concerns NIR and MIR aqueous measurements and tempered sample holders, not an in-line temperature sensor in cell culture; transfer to Raman or a pilot probe is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: In a reactive extraction study, temperature was varied along with concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This could support including temperature as a calibration variable and using an in-line temperature sensor to record it during runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study is on lithium recycling liquid-liquid extraction, not cell culture medium, and the quote does not identify the spectroscopic method or probe.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E02 ¶19

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the review says it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution and complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: For a combined MIR-ATR and Raman option, this suggests testing whether each method adds complementary information before building a fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general PAT review, not a cell-culture study; complementarity must be demonstrated on the actual medium and process.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E01 ¶82

items.finding: A tomato maturity study reports that a multimodal fusion model combining imaging, spectroscopy and haptic sensing surpassed single-modal methods.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the idea of comparing a fused model against the best single method, as the gap notes, but only as a reason to test in the cell-culture context.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is abstract-only and concerns tomato maturity, not glucose or lactate in cell culture; it uses different modalities and deep-learning classification rather than quantitative calibration.

citation.quote: This neural network model achieves 99.4% accuracy in tomato maturity classification, surpassing single-modal methods (color imaging: 94.2%; spectroscopy: 87.8%; haptics: 87.2%).
citation.label: E04 ¶1
